Court No. - 14

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 13027 of 2022
Applicant :- Rashid
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
Counsel for Applicant :- Santosh Srivastava,Sumit Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Pankaj Kumar Shukla Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

Heard Shri Sumit Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the accused/applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as ShriPankaj Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and perused the record.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Rashid for grant of bail, in Complaint Case No. 2102 of 2010, Case Crime No. 227 of 2007, under Sections 376, 506 IPC, Police Station Manikpur, District Pratapgarh, during trial.

Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that the accused-applicant has falsely been implicated in the instant case and he has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the FIR of this case was lodged against the applicant way back in the year 2007 and after investigation, the final report was submitted by the investigating officer.

Thereafter,
a protest petition was filed by the informant, which was treated as complaint by the magistrate court and after recording the statement of the complainant/victim U/s 200 CrPC as well as of witnesses U/s 202 CrPC, the applicant was summoned to face trial.
It is vehemently submitted that the allegations as levelled in the FIR were not found truthful during the course of investigation and even no question was raised by the trial court on submission of final report and the protest petition filed by the informant was treated as complaint.
It is also submitted that there is no medical report in support of the allegation of rape or in support of the allegations of sexual assault.
There is only oral statement of the prosecutrix which has not been believed by the investigating officer, during the course of investigation.

It is next submitted that the summoning order passed by the trial court was challenged by the applicant by filing 482 CrPC application bearing No.5610 of 2012 before this Court in which vide order 22.04.2014, the order of taking no coercive steps against the applicant was passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court.

However, the said 482 CrPC application was dismissed in default on 4.1.2022 and on becoming aware of the dismissal of the said application, non-bailable warrants were issued against the applicant and in execution of the same, the applicant has been arrested and he is in jail since 6.9.2022.
It is further submitted that the truthfulness of the allegations could only be known, during the course of trial.
The applicant is not having any criminal antecedents.
There is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

Learned A.G.A., on the other hand submits that having manner on which the offence has been committed the applicant is not entitled for any relief.
Learned counsel appearing for the opposite party no.2 vehemently submits that it is on account of connivance with the applicant, the medical examination of the prosecutrix or her statement U/s 164 CrPC was not recorded and having regard to the evidence available against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released on bail.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that certain facts of this case are admitted to the parties.
It is admitted that after lodging of the FIR, the final/closure report was submitted by the investigating officer.

It is also not in dispute that after the submission of the final report, a protest petition was filed by the informant, which was treated as complaint and after recording the statement of the prosecutrix and her witnesses, summoning order was passed.
It is not disputed that the said summoning order was challenged by the applicant by filing 482 CrPC application before this Court and on 22.4.2014, an order in favour of the applicant was made.
It is also not in dispute that the said application was dismissed in default on 4.1.2022 and thereafter, coercive processes have been issued against the applicant by the trial court.

It is also not Rashid vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4017191/
2 in dispute that there is no medical examination report of the prosecutrix and no statement of the prosecutrix U/s 164 CrPC has been recorded.

sentences.text: The allegations and counter allegations have been levelled by the parties against each other pertaining to the quality of investigation done by the investigating officer, is a subject matter of trial.
Now, the crux is that the applicant has been summoned in a complaint case, he is in jail in this case since 6.9.2022 without any criminal history.
His presence could be secured before the trial court by placing any adequate conditions.

Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Rashid involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
Observations made herein-above are only for the purpose of disposal of bail application and the same shall not have any bearing on the trial of the case.
